choice: Conformance of generated .okf output is tested with a pinned, vendored copy of okf_validate.py (okf-skills 0.10.1, MIT) under tests/vendor/ run in strict mode, with pyyaml as a dev dependency.
rejected: Depending on okf-skills as an installed or runtime dependency, or writing a custom validator, instead of vendoring a pinned test-only copy.

choice: Handoffs are listed by a function in a new handoffs module (with an okf helper) that the briefing calls and `--json` prints, sharing one 'passed' predicate with review-due so a handoff is in exactly one list and expired ones are excluded.

Defines a single index format for all kmctl verbs: docs/README.md indexes pages, an entry is a list item whose first link is a relative link, concept counts are neither written nor checked, and `kmctl check` reports findings via `--json` as a shared list of check/file/line/message that other checks extend.
rejected: Writing and checking concept counts in indexes (prose counts no script can keep right).

choice: Review-due is computed from OKF's own fields (stale_after, verified, sources with git history), reporting only, and is exposed as a shared function plus a CLI command that always exits 0.
The briefing is implemented as a kmctl command that combines count-only state, packaged knowledge-management rules, and a word-budget test, with a --json output option.

Ship the Claude Code plugin as a plugin/ folder with a manifest, a repo-root marketplace, and a single SessionStart hook that runs `kmctl briefing` and degrades gracefully with an install hint when kmctl is missing.

kmctl ships its plugin inside the wheel as package data (switching build backend to hatchling if needed), copies it to one fixed staging marketplace folder under its data directory on install, and installs via the claude CLI's local marketplace add/update, uninstall, install sequence, verifying with `claude plugin list --json`, rather than installing from GitHub HEAD.
rejected: Installing the plugin from GitHub HEAD (a remote marketplace), which would tie the plugin version to the repository's head rather than the installed kmctl release.

choice: Ship the CI knowledge checks as a composite GitHub Action in the repo that installs kmctl from its own checkout, fails only on `kmctl check`, reports review-due without failing, and unshallows the clone before reading git history.
rejected: Guessing the history-based review reason from a shallow clone.

choice: `kmctl new handoff --key` keys a handoff to the Claude Code session id, so a repeat call with the same key replaces the body and description in place and an unknown key creates a new handoff.
The audit agent is restricted by its tool list to Read, Grep and Glob so audits report findings only and the audit skill runs the CLI itself and passes due concepts to the agent.
rejected: Giving the agent Bash, Edit or Write so it could run kmctl itself or write fixes and findings to files.

choice: Add an opt-in `mode: audit` to the GitHub Action that runs headless Claude Code limited to read-only tools, refuses non-dispatch/schedule events, and reports findings to the job summary and a single 'Knowledge audit' issue.

The CI LLM audit is split into two steps so the model-running step never has a GitHub token in its environment (or persisted checkout credentials), while a separate model-free step holds GH_TOKEN and creates or edits the issue.
rejected: Keeping GH_TOKEN set for the whole audit step and only removing it from claude's own environment, which still leaks via /proc/PID/environ.

choice: The CI audit runs Hermes Agent (pinned to 0.19.0) against any OpenAI-compatible provider, restricted to a custom kmctl_read plugin toolset with three read-only tools, instead of Claude Code with an Anthropic key.
rejected: Claude Code (`claude -p`) with an Anthropic API key, and Hermes' built-in toolsets, which have no read-only option.

choice: kmctl init seeds four packaged knowledge rule files into .claude/rules/ (never overwriting existing files), keeps them as separate package data from the briefing's rules, and writes the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block once per real file, appending or replacing only its own block.
rejected: Adding the two new rules to the briefing's own rules (src/kmctl/rules/), which was ruled out because it would exceed the 600-word budget.

choice: kmctl init writes a CLAUDE.md containing only @AGENTS.md when AGENTS.md exists without a CLAUDE.md, and leaves CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md symlinks that dangle or point outside the repository alone with a warning.
rejected: Writing a CLAUDE.md with the block itself beside AGENTS.md, which would hide AGENTS.md from Claude Code, or writing through unsafe symlinks.

choice: Tests that reach the network are split into an `integration` pytest tier excluded from the default run via `addopts`, run by a separate `integration` gate at every stamp, and retried up to two more times only on network-error output via a home-built conftest hook rather than a new dependency.
rejected: Leaving the network tests in the default run, dropping them from the stamp, or adding a retry plugin dependency such as pytest-rerunfailures.

choice: Document shapes are defined in a single table in src/kmctl/kinds.py that both the writers (kmctl new, new doc, init) and a new `kmctl schema` command read, so the JSON Schema is built from kmctl's own code rather than maintained separately.
rejected: Leaving document shapes implicit in scattered one-line rules, skeleton lists and strings in scaffold.py, with no command that states them (or a separately maintained schema that could drift).

choice: Releases are cut through a hand-run workflow that opens a version pull request and a tag workflow that publishes GitHub Releases only (wheel, sdist, SHA256SUMS, no PyPI), with plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json as the single version source read by hatchling's regex version source.
rejected: hatch-vcs tag-derived versions (they fail in the action's archive checkout without .git) and publishing to PyPI.

choice: Replace the aim package manager (aim.toml and aim.lock.toml) with APM (apm.yml and apm.lock.yaml) for managing the repo's agent rules and skills.
rejected: Keeping aim as the manifest and lockfile tool for agent rules and skills.

choice: Distribute kmctl's skills and agent through APM via a separate meta package at apm/apm.yml that depends on the unmodified plugin/ subfolder and a pinned okf-skills, with no apm.yml inside plugin/, and with the root and apm/ apm.yml version copies kept in sync with the plugin manifest by release.py.
rejected: Putting an apm.yml inside plugin/ (APM would then read agents only from .apm/agents/ and drop the kmctl agent), and exporting kmctl's content from the root apm.yml (which would hand consumers the repo's 16 dev items).

choice: The briefing no longer carries the knowledge rules, only the one rule the rule files lack (treat unverified or stale concepts as leads), because kmctl init writes the rules to .claude/rules/ and they reach the system prompt there; the bundled src/kmctl/rules/ source is removed.
rejected: Keeping the full rules in the briefing alongside the init-written rule files, which duplicated them and kept the briefing at about 600 words.

choice: kmctl init, and its new alias kmctl update, overwrites the four shipped knowledge rule files with the packaged copy on every run, touching only those four names and not tracking user edits.
rejected: Keeping existing rule files, as init did before, and hash-tracking user edits to decide what to overwrite.

choice: kmctl installs only through APM: the skills, agent and knowledge rules ship in one APM package under apm/.apm, and `kmctl plugin install --harness claude` wraps `apm install` and writes the SessionStart hook and okf MCP server itself, replacing the Claude plugin/marketplace route and making apm/apm.yml the single version source.
rejected: Keeping the Claude plugin (plugin/ and marketplace) as a parallel install route, with `kmctl init` writing the rules separately.

choice: Support Antigravity as a second harness by running APM with --target antigravity and then having kmctl write and own a .agents/plugins/kmctl/ plugin folder, with a hook, agents translated from the Claude-format sources at install time, and okf's MCP server pinned by sha.
rejected: Installing okf-skills with `agy plugin install`, which kept Claude-shaped hooks and agents so that agy counted 0 hooks and 0 agents; relying on APM alone, which writes no agents and no MCP config for Antigravity.

choice: Add a read-only, offline `kmctl doctor` verb that checks per harness that dependencies, APM-installed files, hook, okf skills/MCP entry and init files match what this CLI's install writes (sharing the install's builder functions), exits nonzero on failure, and replaces the `kmctl plugin status` verb, which is removed.
rejected: Keeping `kmctl plugin status` (which checks the old claude plugin route) as the checking verb, and running `claude plugin list` or network checks by default.

choice: kmctl plugin install and update prompt interactively for harnesses when --harness is omitted and stdin is a terminal, and refuse with exit 1 (instead of defaulting to claude) when not at a terminal or when --json is given.
rejected: Keeping the silent default to claude when --harness is missing (and guessing in non-interactive runs).

choice: kmctl writes Antigravity's four knowledge rules itself into .agents/plugins/kmctl/rules/ (translated to agy's comma-separated glob front matter) and deletes APM's copies from .agents/rules/ after install, instead of relying on APM to install them.
rejected: Keeping APM's Antigravity writer as the source of the rules (as ADR 0015 says), which emits Windsurf-format files that agy refuses or never matches; APM 0.33.0 is the newest release, so waiting for a fix was not an option.

choice: Replace the Hermes-based CI audit with a single standalone PydanticAI script (action/agent.py, PEP 723 inline deps, run via uv) that supports any provider, context and skill folders, a shell tool with a clean environment, and typed report output kept as an artifact, with GitHub posting in a separate token-holding step.
rejected: Hermes Agent with read-only kmctl tools and the bash/helper scripts (audit-batches.py, audit-report.py, kmctl-read plugin), as decided in ADR 0010.

choice: kmctl takes ownership of okf's Stop hook for Antigravity: after APM's install it removes the okf-stop-check.sh handler from .agents/hooks.json and adds its own kmctl-okf-stop hook in the plugin folder, which continues only on the first stop of a turn and otherwise prints {} and exits 0.
rejected: Leaving APM's .agents/hooks.json handler in place, which fails with exit 127 at the end of every turn because agy runs hooks from the .agents/ folder.

choice: The CI audit is split into an unprivileged audit job that runs the agent and uploads a report artifact, and a separate publish job (with issues: write, caches disabled) that validates the artifact as data and posts or updates one GitHub issue via gh, replacing the shell script, so the token is never given to a job that runs the agent.
rejected: Having the audit job run the agent and post the issue itself with the token (the old action/knowledge-audit-issue.sh in audit mode).

choice: kmctl's APM package is split into three APM packages (shared, claude, antigravity) so APM itself delivers the SessionStart hook, okf's MCP server and the Antigravity rules, and kmctl plugin install stops writing them, keeping only plugin.json and translated agents and cleaning up what it wrote before.
rejected: kmctl writing the SessionStart hook, okf's MCP server and the Antigravity rules itself (as ADR 0014, 0015 and 0016 decided), instead of handing them to APM.

choice: kmctl no longer wraps APM: `kmctl plugin install`, `update` and `remove` are removed, users run `apm install` and `apm uninstall` themselves, and a new `kmctl plugin patch` (with `--undo`) never runs APM and only writes what APM cannot, namely the Antigravity plugin folder and cleanup of older kmctl entries.
rejected: Keeping `kmctl plugin install/update/remove` as wrappers that write apm.yml and run APM for the user (ADR 0014 and ADR 0019).

choice: Keep the generated Antigravity rules in sync with the Claude rules through a local pre-commit hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml, installed by just hooks as pre-commit.local and run after loopctl's gate) that runs scripts/sync_antigravity_rules.py and blocks the commit when the copies change.
rejected: Leaving the sync as a manual step or a CI-only check instead of enforcing it at commit time.

choice: docs/ folder indexes (README.md in each Diataxis folder) are generated by kmctl, enforced by kmctl check as an error with --fix to regenerate, and docs pages carry optional OKF v0.2 front matter (description, stale_after, verified, sources) that review due reads, without making docs/ an OKF bundle; kmctl also ships a pre-commit hook.
rejected: Hand-maintained folder indexes listed in docs/README.md, and treating docs/ as a full OKF bundle.

choice: The CI audit is split into three shipped prompt files (docs-vs-code, okf-vs-code, okf-vs-docs) selected by a new `run --audit NAME` option and run as separate matrix jobs with per-audit artifacts, replacing the single inlined default prompt.
rejected: A single default audit prompt (the audit skill with the auditor's instructions inlined) that checks only concepts that are due.

choice: CI's prek and tests jobs run through the operator's shared JasperHG90/toiminnot GitHub Actions, pinned by commit SHA at v1.3.0, instead of inline commands in ci.yml.
rejected: Keeping the inline prek and pytest commands (with setup-uv and checkout) in ci.yml.

choice: The CI audit agent exports OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP/HTTP to Langfuse (or any OTLP endpoint), opt-in via environment variables, adding pinned opentelemetry-sdk and OTLP exporter dependencies.
rejected: Relying only on transcript.json for reviewing runs, or an always-on or input-configured tracing setup.

choice: The briefing tells the agent to fill in missing init, manifesto and architecture files with the user before other work, exposes this as `setup` in --json, and trims routing text and handoff titles to stay within the 500-token budget.

Add a `kmctl verify ID --by human:<id>` verb that writes a timestamped `verified` entry, only for a named person who has read and confirmed the concept (never on an audit verdict alone), and refuses handoffs and a passed `stale_after` unless `--stale-after` is given.
rejected: Leaving clearance as a hand edit of the front matter YAML, or letting an agent verify a concept on an audit verdict.

choice: OpenCode becomes kmctl's third harness: APM installs the package with --target opencode, and kmctl plugin patch translates the agents into OpenCode's permission format, adds .opencode/rules/*.md to opencode.json's instructions, and writes a .opencode/plugins/kmctl.js plugin for the session briefing, with no apm/opencode sub-package.
rejected: An apm/opencode sub-package, since APM writes neither rules nor hooks for OpenCode; also relying on a plain apm install, which leaves the agents unloadable and the rules and briefing absent.

choice: The kmctl-starter copier template moves into the kmctl repository (copier.yml at root with _subdirectory: starter), versioned by kmctl's release tags, with the release bumping kmctl_ref's default to its own tag and CI bootstrapping the starter from this checkout.
rejected: Keeping the template in a separate kmctl-starter repository that pins kmctl_ref and is bumped by a daily bump-kmctl workflow.

choice: The starter template optionally includes the adversarial-review rule, written into AGENTS.md, and the adversarial reviewer agent installed through APM only for Claude Code, via a new copier question that defaults to yes, with the rule's text copied from a pinned commit of jasperhg90/skills.
rejected: Leaving users to add the reviewer and rule to apm.yml by hand, or installing the rule and agent per harness instead of putting the rule in AGENTS.md, which all three harnesses read.

choice: The kmctl on PATH hands off to the project's pinned kmctl release (by resolved commit through uvx as a child process), just kmctl no longer replaces an existing install, and the briefing reports newer releases from a cached, detached git ls-remote check.
rejected: Having just kmctl force-install the pinned version over the single kmctl on PATH (and pinning by tag through uvx, which takes 2.3 s and fails offline); a shell launcher and os.execvp were also passed over.

choice: The OKF bundle gains a project summary concept capped at 500 words, with its own freshness rule (listed in review due when concepts change after it, cleared by an edit or an agent's `kmctl summary ack`, exempt from unverified/stale_after), forming a progressive-disclosure layer between briefing and section indexes.
rejected: Hooking the summary refresh into every tool call or end of turn with a review_due check, and treating the summary like other concepts under the verify/stale_after rules; the nudge hook was split into separate tickets.

choice: The bundle's summary page changes shape to new sections that synthesise the knowledge holistically (at most 500 words) and link concepts as evidence, with indexes listing them, instead of listing the bundle.

Add a second hook, a PostToolUse hook on Write|Edit|MultiEdit|Bash, that nudges the agent to update .okf/summary.md whenever files in .okf (other than .log) change, using git only and a hash of the last-nudged changed set stored under the git directory.
rejected: Keeping SessionStart as the only hook (ADR 0004), and nudging at the end of a turn rather than on changes to .okf.

choice: Antigravity and OpenCode get the summary nudge right after tool calls, through agy's PostToolUse hook and OpenCode's execute.after plugin hook, both running kmctl summary nudge and neither blocking.
Release workflows that build or publish a release run setup-uv with its cache disabled, so no cache entry written by another job (such as the audit agent's) can reach a release build.
rejected: Keeping setup-uv's default dependency cache in the release workflows for faster builds.

choice: Drop the PostToolUse summary nudge hook and the `kmctl summary nudge` verb, so kmctl ships only the SessionStart briefing hook for all three harnesses.
rejected: Keeping the PostToolUse nudge that ran kmctl summary nudge after tool calls to tell the agent the summary was behind.

choice: Commit the harness files that APM deploys (.github/, .claude/, .agents/, plus shared config like .mcp.json and opencode.json) and gitignore only apm_modules/, so a fresh clone or cloud agent has the skills, rules and briefing hook.
rejected: Gitignoring every file `just bootstrap` installs (the closed PR #16 and issue #15), which would hide shared project config and leave fresh clones without the harness setup.

choice: GitHub Release notes are generated by a script from main's first-parent history (loop merge summaries and other commits) filled into a template and published with --notes-file, instead of GitHub's generated pull-request list.
rejected: gh release create --generate-notes, which lists merged pull requests.

choice: License kmctl under the MIT license, declared in a LICENSE file and in pyproject.toml metadata.

Every `uses:` in the composite action and in knowledge-audit.yml is pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment, and a test enforces this, so a workflow that pins kmctl pins everything the action runs.
rejected: Leaving the inner actions on movable version tags such as @v6 and @v4.

choice: kmctl doctor gains a third check outcome, warn, which prints but does not fail the run (exit 0), and adds a status field of ok, warn or fail to each check in --json, with ok still true for a warning. Missing harness CLIs and unverifiable Antigravity trust now warn instead of failing.
rejected: Keeping those checks as hard failures, or having doctor guess which harness a person uses, or reading the Antigravity IDE's trust settings.

choice: kmctl review due finds the verification commit as the oldest commit whose front matter holds the newest verified[].at, then compares content with git diff against HEAD instead of comparing committer dates, and adds an 'edited after verification' reason for changes outside verified and stale_after.
rejected: Comparing committer dates, which squash and rebase merges rewrite to merge time, and ignoring edits to the page's own text after verification.

choice: Rename kmctl's okf MCP server from okf-bundle to bundle (dropping drop_old_mcp and any legacy-name handling) so apm audit --ci's lockfile check passes, and gate drift in CI with a frozen-install recipe (apm install --frozen, kmctl plugin patch, fail on non-empty git status --porcelain) instead of apm audit --ci for Antigravity.
rejected: Keeping the okf-bundle name with apm audit --ci as the gate (or --no-drift), and keeping a legacy-name cleanup for older kmctl installs; also adding the gate to the starter CI workflow.

choice: License kmctl under the MIT license by adding a LICENSE file and declaring it in pyproject.toml.
Releases are produced by CI and always carry release notes, written down as a project rule in .claude/rules/releases.md.

kmctl's own repository adopts the JasperHG90/toiminnot Hermes GitHub Actions for /hermes comment replies and new-issue triage, triggered by /hermes (never @hermes), with triage comments capped at about 200 tokens by a prompt short form and a truncating apply script with a label allowlist.
rejected: Porting the workflows to the standalone action/agent.py PydanticAI script (ADR 0017), and triggering on @hermes.

choice: kmctl check reports a summary over the 500-word limit as a warning instead of an error, and a new --strict flag makes warnings fail the check.
rejected: Keeping the word limit as a hard error that always fails kmctl check.

choice: kmctl audit ui serves a local review page on 127.0.0.1 where a person rates claims and checks, and feedback is appended to a SQLite file at .kmctl/audit.sqlite.

The audit moves out of kmctl into its own uv workspace member package, kmaudit, with its own CLI and its own copy of the front matter helpers, so it runs without kmctl and kmctl loses its audit group and extra.
rejected: Keeping the audit inside kmctl as an optional extra and importing kmctl's okf and tracing modules, or splitting the repository instead of using a workspace member beside the root kmctl.

choice: kmaudit audits any folder of markdown docs, with each folder as its own namespace (path relative to the repo root) stored in a separate SQLite file under .kmaudit/ at the repository root, and the old .kmctl/audit.sqlite is copied into the .okf namespace on first open.
rejected: One shared store (.kmctl/audit.sqlite) for the whole repository, where folders would share sections, claims and checks.

choice: kmaudit gets a read-only `briefing` verb that a SessionStart hook injects. It opens each store with SQLite `mode=ro` instead of `Store`, never migrates, and always exits 0.
rejected: Opening the store through `Store`, which creates `.kmaudit/` and migrates the schema, and SQLite `immutable=1`, which gives wrong counts while agents write.

choice: kmaudit's main interface is a stdio MCP server (`kmaudit mcp`) built on the official MCP Python SDK, with tools mirroring the verbs, instead of agents shelling out to a CLI.
rejected: Agents driving the audit by shelling out to the CLI.

choice: Move kmctl into packages/kmctl as its own buildable package and make the repo root a non-installing uv virtual workspace (one root uv.lock, members packages/*), with install URLs for post-move releases using #subdirectory=packages/kmctl and a root hatchling stub build-system so pre-commit can install the hook repo.
rejected: Keeping kmctl as the root package (root layout, installed from the repo root) alongside packages/kmaudit.

choice: Split the CI workflow into one test job per package (kmctl, kmaudit, repo), plus a `tests` collector job with `if: always()` that keeps main's required `tests` check reporting, and add a test that keeps the CI job directories in step with the loop's root `uv run pytest` gate.
rejected: Changing main's ruleset to require the new per-package jobs instead of adding a collecting `tests` job.

choice: Release kmctl or kmaudit independently from one Release workflow, each with its own version source (kmaudit via a dynamic hatchling regex VERSION file), its own tag family (kmctl keeps vX.Y.Z, kmaudit uses kmaudit-vX.Y.Z), and path-filtered release notes drafted and committed in the version PR that release-tag publishes unchanged, with only kmctl marked Latest.
rejected: A single shared version and tag family for both packages, and a static kmaudit version in pyproject.toml (which would require re-locking uv.lock on every bump); also rewriting notes in release-tag instead of reviewing them in the PR.

choice: The release run has Hermes (all tools disabled) rewrite only the What changed section of the deterministic notes draft, and a script keeps the rewrite only if headings, the sections after What changed, and the set of references match the draft, otherwise the draft stands, with the merging reviewer as the guard on meaning.
rejected: Letting Hermes rewrite the whole notes file or run with tools enabled, and failing the release run when Hermes errors or returns an invalid rewrite, instead of falling back to the deterministic draft.

choice: The cutoff for installing kmctl from #subdirectory=packages/kmctl moves from v0.12.1 to v0.12.2, held in one constant, LAST_ROOT_RELEASE, with one helper deciding the fragment.

Each package keeps its own APM package and version source in its folder (packages/kmctl/apm and packages/kmaudit/apm, with the version in apm.yml), replacing the root apm/ and kmaudit's VERSION file; consumers' entries change to path: packages/kmctl/apm after a release cutoff.
rejected: Leaving kmctl's APM package at the repository root in apm/ and giving kmaudit a VERSION file as its version source.

choice: kmaudit's skills and agents move into kmaudit's own APM package (agents in a Claude-only sub-package) and drive kmaudit through its MCP tools instead of the shell, with the package declaring the kmaudit MCP server pinned to its release, and Antigravity and OpenCode get the skills and server but no agents.
rejected: Keeping the skills and agents in kmctl's package driving kmaudit through the CLI and guard hook, and teaching kmctl's plugin patch to translate kmaudit's agents for Antigravity and OpenCode.

choice: kmaudit's CLI is cut to mcp, ui, namespaces, briefing and the claims and checks list commands, with every other verb (and the guard hook) removed and reachable only as an MCP tool or Python function, and reruns of stale checks move to a UI button backed by a POST /api/rerun endpoint.
rejected: Keeping the full verb set on the CLI alongside the MCP tools, with agents driving kmaudit through the shell and the guard hook.

choice: The root README becomes a short map to per-package READMEs, which carry each package's install and use, and all reference docs live in the root docs/, with kmaudit's pages named kmaudit-* and owned by kmaudit rather than kmctl.
rejected: Keeping kmctl's whole manual in the root README and leaving kmaudit's command reference in packages/kmaudit/docs/.
